issue_context.title: ChannelReader.ReadAsync/ChannelWriter.WriteAsync don't return or throw when cancellation token is signaled
comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).
Do you still see this with .NET 6?

@stephentoub  I have not tried because I'm using VS2019 and my understanding per the docs is that .NET 6 requires VS2022... if it would help you analyze I can try to set up a .NET 6 environment independent of VS, but I would hope to be able to use .NET 5/VS2019 for this project in the long run...

> if it would help you analyze I can try to set up a .NET 6 environment independent of VS

I tried your repro, and while I see the reported results with .NET 5, it runs to completion successfully on .NET 6.

> FYI, end of support for .NET 5 is May 8th. https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core
> 
> I tried your repro, and while I see the reported results with .NET 5, it runs to completion successfully on .NET 6.

@stephentoub  Thanks for that heads up.  It had not clicked with me that .NET 5 was only a 1.5 year lifecycle.  It sounds like this won't be fixed in 5.0, but do you have any idea what is causing this behavior?  I'm hoping for some reassurance that calling Complete is a reliable workaround in the absence of the token actually canceling the operation.

Thank you for the further explanation.  I'm a long time kernel programmer but a .NET novice, so I'm happy to accept the user error label here.  The part that surprises me is that I would have expected the signaling of the token being canceled to impact all tasks simultaneously - like multiple threads waiting on a common event in win32.  But it sounds like the cancelation needs to propagate through synchronously from task to task performing each of their continuations serially?  Or did I misunderstand your analysis?

> I'm happy to accept the user error label here

I didn't mean to imply you did anything wrong, apologies.  I was trying to say that the components are behaving the way they were designed to, but the confluence of those designs is leading to an issue that violates what a user can reasonably expect, and so is an issue we should consider fixing.

> But it sounds like the cancelation needs to propagate through synchronously from task to task performing each of their continuations serially?

Effectively, yes.  CancellationToken.Register hooks up a callback that's invoked when the associated CancellationTokenSource.Cancel method is called.  All such registrations with the same token source are invoked synchronously one after the other (that's generally how events work in .NET, and this is basically an event, just with a different syntax).
No worries, no offense taken.  Again, really appreciate the responsiveness on all of this.
